裂縫鼓在非洲、東南亞與大洋洲見於傳統與生活場合。非洲常置於河流或山谷等有利傳音處: Slit drums appear in traditional and everyday settings in Africa, Southeast Asia and Oceania. In Africa they are often placed where sound carries, such as by a river or in a valley, for long-distance communication; the kentongan of Java, Indonesia, is used to wake people for the pre-dawn meal in Ramadan; in Vanuatu they are made from large logs, and on some islands they are set upright and carved with spirit figures, becoming one of the national symbols.
裂縫鼓屬體鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 111.243。演奏時: The slit drum is an idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.243. It is played by striking the edge of the slit with a stick or beater so that the whole hollow body of wood or bamboo vibrates; where the slit cuts out tongues, tongues of different area or thickness give different pitches. The closed ends form a resonating chamber and the sound comes out through the opening; when the size of the chamber matches the pitch, the sound is produced more efficiently and is louder. A beginner can first find the slit or the tongues, then strike near the edge with a stick and listen to the sound coming out of the chamber.
裂縫鼓的琴身與發聲體主要為木或竹，通常由竹材或木料鑿刻、組合成近似封閉的中空共鳴: The body and sounding material of the slit drum are mainly wood or bamboo. It is usually carved and assembled from bamboo or timber into a nearly closed hollow resonating chamber, with one or more slits cut in the wall and tongues left around the slit as the sounding part. Similar instruments in Vanuatu are made from large logs. It is struck with a stick or beater, though the source does not state their material; the materials of other parts, of surface decoration or of the fixings are not described either.
裂縫鼓的聲音來自木或竹製空心腔體上裂縫邊緣的舌片受擊振動，整體樂器而非鼓膜發聲。: The sound of a slit drum comes from the tongues at the edge of the slit vibrating when struck, in a hollow body of wood or bamboo; the instrument as a whole sounds, not a drumhead. Tongues of different area or thickness give different pitches, and most instruments have one slit, though some have two or three slits forming several tongues. The body closed at both ends acts as a soundbox and the sound leaves through the opening; when the volume of the body matches the pitch of the tongues the instrument speaks more efficiently and louder. It is played by striking the edge of the slit with a stick or beater, and the volume depends on the volume of the resonating chamber. Unlike a true drum with a head, its spread of pitches comes from the thickness of the tongues and the design of the body rather than from a vibrating membrane.
裂縫鼓起源於非洲、太平洋島嶼和東南亞等地區，是人類最古老的打擊樂器之一。這種樂器: The slit drum originated in Africa, the Pacific islands and Southeast Asia and is one of the oldest percussion instruments. It appeared in ancient times, first made by local peoples from natural timber or bamboo and used for communication, ritual and entertainment. In traditional African cultures the slit drum was often used to carry messages over long distances, because its distinctive timbre cuts through the bush; on the Pacific islands it was closely tied to religious ritual and community activity. Through the cultural exchange of the colonial period the slit drum spread gradually around the world. In modern times it has been widely studied by ethnomusicologists and holds an important place in world music performance, embodying the musical knowledge and cultural identity of different civilisations.

A slit drum is a hollow struck idiophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 111.243. It is mostly made of bamboo or wood, with a largely closed resonating chamber whose surface has one or more slits; it is played by striking the edge of the slit with a stick or beater. In some designs the cut is made on three sides, leaving one side as a tongue, and tongues of different area or thickness give different pitches. Instruments of this kind are found in Africa, Southeast Asia and Oceania; in Africa they are often placed in river valleys and similar spots for long-distance communication, while in Vanuatu they are made from large logs, and on the central islands the drums stand upright and are decorated with carvings of spirits.
